prompt.context: This is a market sizing question about one of the world's busiest airports.
prompt.question: How many passengers go through Heathrow each year?

clarifying_info.q: What is the average passenger capacity of the planes (arrivals and departures)?
Is a 75% load factor a fair assumption?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, 75% load factor is a reasonable assumption.

framework: Define scope: passengers = arrivals + departures (note transient/connecting passengers may be double-counted)
Estimate flight frequency: planes landing and departing
Estimate airport operating hours per day and days per year
Estimate average plane capacity and load factor
Multiply through to get annual passenger volume
Sanity-check result and flag double-counting issue for connecting passengers

questions.prompt: Estimate the number of passengers passing through Heathrow in a year.
questions.guidance: Candidate should build up the estimate step by step: flight frequency, operating hours, capacity, and load factor. A strong candidate proactively flags the double-counting issue for transient/connecting passengers (the same passenger both arrives and departs). Process and logical structure matter more than arriving at the exact real-world number.

math.setup: Flights per hour x operating hours per day x days per year x passengers per flight = annual passengers
steps: Assume 1 landing + 1 departure every 30 seconds = 2 movements per 30 sec = 4 movements per minute = 240 movements per hour
Flights per year: 120 x 21 x 365 = 919,800 arriving flights (same for departing)
Passengers per flight: 200 capacity x 75% load = 150 passengers
Note: if transient passengers are counted in both arrivals and departures, this double-counts them — flag this to the interviewer
math.answer: Approximately 138 million arriving passengers per year (or ~276 million total movements if counting both arrivals and departures); flag double-counting of connecting passengers

recommendation: Heathrow handles on the order of 100-140 million one-way passenger trips per year based on reasonable assumptions about flight frequency, operating hours, load factor, and aircraft size
Process: estimate flights per hour from movement frequency, scale to annual hours, apply load factor to get passenger count
risks: Double-counting transient/connecting passengers who appear in both arrival and departure figures
Actual operating hours or load factors may differ significantly from assumptions
Fleet mix (narrow-body vs. wide-body) affects average capacity
next_steps: Cross-check estimate against known benchmarks (Heathrow historically handles ~60-80 million terminal passengers per year in reality, so estimates in that order of magnitude are reasonable)
Clarify whether the question asks for terminal passengers only or total passenger movements including transits
